'''''Vicia tenuifolia''''', the '''fine-leaved vetch,''' '''cow vetch''',<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Vicia tenuifolia Fine-Leaved Vetch, Cow vetch PFAF Plant Database|url=https://pfaf.org/user/Plant.aspx?LatinName=Vicia+tenuifolia|access-date=2021-08-27|website=pfaf.org}}</ref> '''fodder vetch'''<ref>{{Cite web|date=2019-07-21|title=Vicia tenuifolia|url=https://plantsbank.com/vicia-tenuifolia/|access-date=2021-08-27|website=PlantsBank|language=en-US}}</ref> or '''bramble vetch''',<ref name=":1" /> is a [[Herbaceous plant|herbaceous]] [[Perennial plant|perennial]] plant species in the family [[Fabaceae]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Drobnolistna grašica – Urbanatura|url=https://www.urbanatura.si/vsebina/1252|access-date=2021-08-26|website=www.urbanatura.si|language=sl}}</ref> This species is widespread in [[Europe]] and some parts of both [[Asia]] and [[Africa]]. In some other areas it occurs as an introduced species.<ref name=":1" /> In a few countries this edible vetch is used as food for both humans and farm animals.<ref name=":0" />

== Taxonomy ==
''Vicia tenuifolia'' was described by German botanist [[Albrecht Wilhelm Roth]] in his work Tentamen florae germanicae in 1788.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=Vicia tenuifolia Roth|url=https://www.gbif.org/species/2975188|access-date=2021-08-27|website=www.gbif.org|language=en}}</ref> Some taxonomists treat this species as a subspecies of ''[[Vicia cracca]]'', while most recognize it as its own species.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Vicia tenuifolia {{!}} Online Atlas of the British and Irish Flora |url=https://plantatlas2020.org/atlas/2cd4p9h.9cy |access-date=2021-08-27 |website=www.brc.ac.uk |language=en}}</ref>

There are a few recognized subspecies:<ref name=":3" />

* ''Vicia tenuifolia'' subsp. ''atroviolacea'' ([[Bornm.]]) Greuter & Burdet
* ''Vicia tenuifolia'' subsp. ''delmasii'' ([[Emb.]] & Maire) Dobignard
* ''Vicia tenuifolia'' subsp. ''subalpina'' ([[Grossh.]]) Zernov
* ''Vicia tenuifolia'' subsp. ''tenuifolia''
* ''Vicia tenuifolia'' subsp. ''variabilis'' ([[Freyn]] & [[Sint.]]) [[Dinsm.]]
* ''Vicia tenuifolia'' subsp. ''villosa'' ([[Batt.]]) Greuter

== Description ==
This herbaceous and perennial [[legume]] can reach from 30 to 150 centimetres of height. It is usually an upright-growing and spread out [[vetch]] with rough stem that is either hairless or hirsute.<ref name=":0" /> As with many other pea family species, ''Vicia tenuifolia'' is a [[Nitrogen fixation|nitrogen-fixing]] plant.<ref name=":2" />

Its alternately arranged leaves are [[pinnately compound]] and most of the times consist of 10–18 pairs of narrowly linear to [[Oblong leaf|oblong]] leaflets.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":6">{{Cite web|title=Fine-leaved vetch (Vicia tenuifolia) – Plants {{!}} Candide Gardening|url=https://candidegardening.com/GB/plants/14cf92cc-0e14-40a5-858b-18d3aa740479|access-date=2021-08-27|website=Candide|language=en-GB|archive-date=2021-08-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210827082420/https://candidegardening.com/GB/plants/14cf92cc-0e14-40a5-858b-18d3aa740479|url-status=dead}}</ref> Pinna can be both hirsute or hairless and usually measure from 2 to 6 millimetres. ''Vicia tenuifolia'' has so called [[paripinnate]] leaves, that end with a split [[tendril]]. Stipules are present; they are narrowly linear, with entire leaf margin and end with a sharpened point.<ref name=":0" />

The species is an [[entomophilous]] plant<ref name=":2" /> and flowers between June and August.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Vicia cracca subsp. tenuifolia|url=https://www.infoflora.ch/de/flora/vicia-cracca-subsp-tenuifolia.html|access-date=2021-08-27|website=www.infoflora.ch}}</ref> ''Vicia tenuifolia'' has typical [[bilaterally symmetrical]] [[papilionaceous flower|papilionaceous flowers]], that consists of a banner, keel and wing, with the flower's [[petal]]s being red, pink or blueish purple. The biggest petal – the so-called banner – is brighter than other petals, with its limb being as long as its claw.<ref name=":0" /> From 15 to 30 small flowers are arranged into an [[raceme]] inflorescence,<ref name=":6" /> that has long leafstalk (the latter is usually twice as long as the inflorescence). The flower's [[sepal]]s are fused together into a few millimetres long calyx tube that ends with 5 short calyx tooth. Each flower has 10 anthers; the latter are fused together till the last third of anther's length.<ref name=":0" />

This species' dried fruit is a brownish and hairless [[legume]] that can measure from 3 to 5 centimetres.<ref name=":0" />

''Vicia grandiflora'' can be confused with the similar vetch species ''[[Vicia dalmatica]]'', ''[[Vicia cracca]]'', ''[[Vicia incana]]'' and ''[[Vicia villosa]]''.<ref name=":0" />

== Distribution and conservation ==
This vetch species is widely distributed across Europe (especially the Euro-Mediterranean region,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Vicia tenuifolia (VICTF)[Overview]{{!}} EPPO Global Database|url=https://gd.eppo.int/taxon/VICTF|access-date=2021-08-27|website=gd.eppo.int}}</ref> south and central Europe<ref name=":5">{{Cite web|date=2017-10-17|title=Vicia tenuifolia Roth|url=https://www.cwrnl.nl/en/CWRnl-1/CWRbyname/Vicia-tenuifolia-Roth-1.htm|access-date=2021-08-27|website=pgrportal.nl|language=en-us}}</ref>) and occurs also in some parts of Asia (usually those that are either temperate either tropical,<ref name=":1" /> mostly southwestern and central Asia<ref name=":5" />), as well as in northern Africa.<ref name=":1" /> In north-western Europe it is not a native species.<ref name=":4" /> ''Vicia tenuifolia'' was once [[Introduced species|introduced]] to [[Hawaii]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=Lopez Poveda|first=Lucia|date=2010-08-03|title=IUCN Red List of Threatened Species: Vicia tenuifolia|url=https://www.iucnredlist.org/en|access-date=2021-08-27|website=IUCN Red List of Threatened Species}}</ref> In some areas it is treated as an [[invasive species]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Vicia tenuifolia|url=https://www.cabi.org/isc/datasheet/117852|access-date=2021-08-27|website=www.cabi.org}}</ref>

''Vicia tenuifolia'' usually grows in a variety of habitats, which can include both natural and [[urban area]]s.<ref name=":0" /> This vetch is mostly an inhabitant of lowlands,<ref name=":4" /> where it can be found in dry meadows and forest edges, as well as on grassy banks, verges or waste ground, especially near railways,<ref name=":4" /> where it is a [[Ruderal species|ruderal]] species.<ref name=":0" /> ''V. tenuifolia'' rarely occurs in uplands, with its maximum elevation being around 2,900 metres.<ref name=":1" />

This species is listed as [[Least-concern species|least concern]] (LC) species on the [[IUCN Red List|IUCN Red list]], with its population being rated as stable.<ref name=":1" />
